gating_order_doc58_SS16_3_step10: anchors -> floors -> rescue_full / rescue_partial per cell -> positive_control_degrades -> SS8's descriptives. NO CONTRAST IS READ PAST A MISSING OR FAILED FLOOR.

positive_control.reading: doc 58 SS9.4 / SS15.1: a rescue procedure that DEGRADES a healthy arm by more than 0.06 is FLAGGED, and every rescue read under that procedure is read with suspicion and reported WITH THE FLAG ATTACHED IN THE SAME SENTENCE. It is NOT a kill switch -- it is a warning that travels (exp43c precedent, doc 24 SS5.2: a control that cannot fail is not a control).
positive_control.no_floor_doc58_SS15_2: the control carries NO floor and that is a decision, not an omission: it is a DEGRADATION CHECK against a committed value, not a gain claim, and doc 52 SS3's 'a gain criterion needs a null' does not bind a loss check.

floors_doc58_SS14.stage1_is_orientation_only: doc 58 SS14.1: all rescue arms are compared FIRST to the committed matched floors. THIS COMPARISON CARRIES NO VERDICT. Its sole function is to decide which cells go to stage 2.
floors_doc58_SS14.stage2_trigger_doc58_SS14_2: any cell whose held-out mean reaches its rescue_partial bar (I1 >= 0.864667, I2 >= 0.823333) TRIGGERS a matched floor RE-RUN UNDER THAT RESCUE PROCEDURE. A cell that does not reach its partial bar cannot pass either boolean regardless of its floor.

severed_donor_protocol_doc58_SS14_4.rule: a warm start injects information through the INITIALISATION, so THE DONOR'S LABELS ARE SEVERED TOO: the T = 1 donor arm is retrained on the shuffled bearer designation at the committed T = 1 recipe (150 epochs), its checkpoint is selected on the SHUFFLED val accuracy, and the shuffled T = 2 run is warm-started from it.
severed_donor_protocol_doc58_SS14_4.seed_linkage: REGISTERED: floor seed k's shuffle RNG seed drives BOTH the T = 1 donor's per-pair reassignment AND the T = 2 run's -- one seed, two item sets.
severed_donor_protocol_doc58_SS14_4.BUILD_LEVEL_OPERATIONALISATION_FLAGGED_F: doc 58 SS14.4 registers BOTH a five-seed donor retraining AND seed linkage, and the two only close under one reading: the T = 2 floor run at seed k is warm-started from THE DONOR TRAINED AT SEED k UNDER SHUFFLE SEED k. That reading is the only one consistent with SS15.3's count of 5 donor runs per cell AND with the committed per-seed S-shuffle construction; under it, step 2's 'select the donor on the SHUFFLED val accuracy' is the WITHIN-RUN checkpoint selection (the content that matters: no true label reaches the initialisation) and the cross-seed lowest-index tie-break is inert. A cross-seed donor selection would either break the linkage or cost 25 donor runs per cell, neither of which is registered. THIS IS A BUILD-LEVEL RESOLUTION OF A REGISTERED AMBIGUITY AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN BURIED.

floors_doc58_SS14.gating_order_doc58_SS14_5: stage-1 mean -> trigger test -> stage-2 floor if triggered -> ONLY THEN the booleans. A TRIGGERED CELL WHOSE FLOOR HAS NOT BEEN RUN HAS NO VERDICT and its booleans are stored as null, NEVER FALSE.
floors_doc58_SS14.sd_readings_doc58_SS9_3: 'clears its procedure-matched floor by >= 2 SD' uses the FLOOR'S OWN SD AS PRIMARY, with all three readings (floor SD, arm SD, pooled) computed and reported, and an arm whose readings DISAGREE reported as disagreeing rather than resolved silently.

directional_call_doc58_SS9_6.rationale_doc58_SS9_6: the same-family T = 1 solution EXISTS, at 0.9820, on the identical features, identical architecture and identical 264-parameter set. If composition is a FINE-TUNING problem rather than a representation problem, the T = 1 optimum is the initialisation most likely to sit in the T = 2 basin's neighbourhood. External support: arXiv:2409.08777 reports avoiding barren plateaus in DisCoCirc by pretraining components. The call is CONFINED to the warm-start cell because the in-programme precedents cut the other way for budget-type levers (doc 38 / exp54: 2.5x budget did not rescue) and because doc 58 SS4.3's own literature registers the failure mode -- transfer into a dissimilar basin -- that SS6.4.3 shows this transfer is exposed to.
directional_call_doc58_SS9_6.if_it_lands_doc58_SS10: composition is a FINE-TUNING problem for the product register: the T = 1 solution is in the T = 2 basin's neighbourhood and standard training simply does not find it from a cold start. THIS WOULD BE THE RUN'S HEADLINE -- and it MAY NOT BE CLAIMED ON THE FIRST DRAW ALONE. The confirm draw at generator seed + 1000 with ALL ARMS OF I1 PRESENT (its anchor and all four rescues), plus doc 58 SS16.2's RETRAINED DONOR, is MANDATORY (doc 47 SS18, doc 58 SS16.3 step 11). Not a statement about DisCoCirc's expressive limits, and not about I2.
directional_call_doc58_SS9_6.every_other_cell: NO DIRECTION REGISTERED -- stated as ignorance, not as a hedge (doc 58 SS9.6). 15 booleans.

bug_hunt_doc58_SS9_5.reason: doc 58 SS9.5, orchestrator ruling 5 (KEPT and stored as inert -- a documented cannot-fire beats an absent row). The gate fires when an arm exceeds its context bound by > 0.06. BOTH instances' per-twin bounds are 1.0000 (doc 55 SS12 for F2, doc 56 SS10 for N-in), so bound + 0.06 > 1 and NO achievable accuracy can trigger it. The positive control's FA bound of record is 0.9625, so its gate would fire above 1.0225 -- also unreachable. mechanism_question_doc58_SS8_2: DOES A SUCCESSFUL RESCUE RESTORE THE q-ASYMMETRY UNDO SIGNATURE TO THE HEALTHY ARMS' PROFILE? Descriptive, NO boolean, NO criterion, and it may NOT be promoted onto a criterion after results exist (the exp44 no-promotion clause). The healthy profile is committed (doc 55 SS20.5): on correct q = 2 items the readout restores per-wire purity to its post-event-1 level (R2-A 0.8755 vs 0.8751); on q = 1 items it does not (0.8017 vs 0.8953). doc 56 SS15.2's amendment applies to I2: for the ENTANGLED arms the restoration target is the INTRO purity, not 1. Reported per arm, stratified by q and by correctness, in `reported_not_registered_doc58_SS9_7[<cell>].purity_doc58_SS8`, on every rescue arm AND both anchors.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: COMPOSITION IS A FINE-TUNING PROBLEM FOR THE PRODUCT REGISTER: the T = 1 solution is in the T = 2 basin's neighbourhood and standard training simply does not find it from a cold start. This would be the run's headline.
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: MAY NOT BE CLAIMED ON THE FIRST DRAW ALONE -- the confirm draw at generator seed + 1000 with ALL ARMS OF I1 PRESENT, plus SS16.2's RETRAINED DONOR, is MANDATORY. Not a statement about DisCoCirc's expressive limits, and not about I2.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.branch: warm-start rescues I1 but NOT I2
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: THE ENTANGLEMENT FAILURE IS DEEPER THAN COMPOSITION WARM-UP. Two encodings, same warm-start intervention, opposite outcomes => I2's failure is not merely 'the T = 2 basin is hard to reach from cold'. Reads onto doc 58 SS4.4's entanglement-induced-plateau mechanism and is exactly the branch doc 56 SS2 query 1 predicted would be different in kind.
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: may NOT be reported as 'entanglement causes barren plateaus' -- one encoding, one gate, one inventory, 4 qubits.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.branch: R-layerwise rescues while R-budget does not
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: STAGED OPTIMISATION FINDS WHAT FULL-PARAMETER OPTIMISATION DOES NOT, and the raw 1.5x epoch excess is NOT the explanation because 3.0x did not rescue (SS6.3.2's guard, registered in advance).
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: not a result about Skolik et al.'s published circuit-GROWING procedure (SS4.2's adaptation clause).

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.branch: R-identity rescues while others do not
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: THE FAILURE IS AN INITIALISATION-BASIN FAILURE: the committed uniform-[0, 2pi) init lands the optimiser somewhere it cannot leave, and limiting effective depth at the first update is sufficient.
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: not a claim that the instance was in a barren plateau -- this is a 4-qubit circuit and no gradient-variance scaling was measured.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.branch: NOTHING RESCUES (all 16 booleans FALSE, floors matched)
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: THE WALLS ARE OPTIMISER-ROBUST AT THIS BUDGET CLASS. Four independent mitigations, one of them a 3x budget with a decay schedule, all fail on instances whose information content is CERTIFIED EXTRACTABLE. THIS STRENGTHENS THE TESTBED'S VALUE: exp72 becomes an instance the mitigation literature does not have (SS4.6), and the honest write-up sentence is 'these four operationalisations, at this budget class, on these two instances, did not convert certified-extractable information.'
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: MAY NOT BE REPORTED AS AN IMPOSSIBILITY. Not 'the circuit cannot learn this'; not 'trainability mitigations do not work'; not 'barren plateaus are unfixable'. Four procedures at one budget class on two instances is A RECORD, NOT A THEOREM, and doc 54 SS17.3's language binds.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: THE PROCEDURE IS FITTING THE SPLIT, NOT THE LABELS. The rescue is NOT READ; the cell is reported as FLOOR-CONTAMINATED with both numbers.
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: no rescue claim of any kind from that cell.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: the procedure DAMAGES a healthy arm. Every rescue under that procedure is reported WITH THE FLAG ATTACHED and read with suspicion (exp43c precedent, doc 24 SS5.2: a control that cannot fail is not a control).
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: a rescue under a flagged procedure may not be reported without the flag in the same sentence.

outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.registered_reading: reported as NO PATTERN FOUND, with all 16 booleans and their per-seed values. At 5 seeds and 8 cells this is a genuinely likely outcome and is registered as an outcome, not as a failure of the experiment.
outcome_rows_doc58_SS10.may_not_be_claimed: no post-hoc narrative may be constructed over the pattern (SS9.8c: no ranking of the four procedures as a criterion).

scope_doc58_SS12: NO QUANTUM READING OF ANY KIND. The comparators are already at 1.0000 on both instances; there is nothing for a circuit to win. exp72 is about OPTIMISATION and only optimisation, and NO EXP72 NUMBER MAY APPEAR IN A SENTENCE CONTAINING 'ADVANTAGE'.

NOT A STATEMENT ABOUT BARREN PLATEAUS. These are 4-qubit circuits. No gradient-variance-versus-qubit-count scaling is measured, and doc 58 SS4.4 / SS4.5's asymptotic results are cited as MECHANISM LANGUAGE, never as diagnoses of these instances.

'THE FIELD'S MITIGATIONS' MEANS EXACTLY THESE FOUR OPERATIONALISATIONS, not the literature's every variant. Noted, not run: full barren-plateau-aware initialisation schemes (beta / Gaussian / reduced-domain / He / Xavier, and the CNN- and RL-based initialisers); quantum natural gradient; SGLD and other noisy/stochastic-gradient optimisers; encoding-entanglement reduction; cost-function locality; circuit-growing layerwise learning in Skolik et al.'s published form; the R-budget budget/schedule decomposition. A NULL ON THESE FOUR IS NOT A NULL ON THOSE.
One dataset, one task family, one category, one surface, two referents, two events, 24 nouns, simulation. doc 50 SS7's ceiling stands.

NOT 'MEANING', not composition-in-general, not DisCoCirc's expressive limits. A rescue relocates a failure from 'training' to 'training with a better recipe'; a null relocates nothing. Neither touches representability -- the bounds are 1.0000 in both cases and always were.
Not novel-filler generalisation; exp69's held-out-PAIRING split, inherited.
R-layerwise is an ADAPTATION of arXiv:2006.14904, not a replication (SS4.2). A null on it says NOTHING about their published circuit-growing method.
what_this_could_not_resolve_doc58_SS19: The four procedures are not exhaustive and are not a random sample of the literature. exp72 runs one initialisation strategy, one staging strategy, one transfer strategy and one budget control.
R-layerwise is an adaptation, not a replication -- stated twice because it is the easiest sentence in the write-up to get wrong.

The one directional call rests on an EXISTENCE argument, not a precedent. This programme has never run a warm start; doc 38 / exp54's budget extension is the only in-programme rescue-shaped intervention and IT FAILED.
Stage 2's cost is conditional and could be zero. If no cell reaches its partial bar, no procedure-matched floor is ever run and doc 58's most careful section is never exercised.
The purity signature is DESCRIPTIVE and under-powered as a mechanism: with 5 seeds and two instances a restored q-asymmetry would be suggestive and nothing more.

What a null actually bounds is hard to state precisely. 'Optimiser-robust at this budget class' means four procedures, one of them 3x the budget with a decay schedule, on two instances, at 5 seeds, at n_test = 300. IT IS A RECORD. IT IS NOT A THEOREM.
